title: Guide/example for creating plugins
body:
Dronecore is the officially supported layer for providing access to PX4, via MAVLink (of course there are other integration points, like the RTSP bridge). We're expecting others to extend the API via plugins, for example, to add support for peripherals that interact with the system via custom MAVLink messages.

We need a simple but realistic example of a plugin and an associated guide that shows how it works/what you need to do to write one.

comments.body: I can't believe MAVLink are only letting us have six cameras https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_COMP_ID_CAMERA :-)

@julianoes 
>I disagree with these API's though because the component ids don't really need to be exposed.

If application is interested in a particular camera (say, downward facing camera), then it needs to be differentiated it by unique camera ID. Can't we use component IDs as camera IDs to differentiate ?

Suppose that a system(vehicle) has 6 cameras, an application may access to camera 1 & 2 as below:
```cpp
DroneCore dc;
...
auto camera_ids = dc.camera_ids(); // similar to device_uuids() method.

// Assuming we've have Camera plugin which is instantiated as below:
auto camera1 = std::make_shared<Camera>(&dc.camera(camera_ids[0]); // access to camera 1
auto camera2 = std::make_shared<Camera>(&dc.camera(camera_ids[1]); // access to camera 2
...
```

I think the API needs to be as simple and clean as possible and therefore I push back on complexity unless absolutely needed. DroneCore could allow to access different cameras but it should be an abstracted API and not the mavlink one.

Ok I agree to keep API as much simple possible. I want to understand what is the complexity in above code.
With current DroneCore interface, we query the device UUIDs that are connected. As we know UUID is per vehicle or system, we need a scheme to distinguish components in a system. If you prefer not to use MAVLink component id, what is the alternative?
We query the devices by UUID. We need to change this so that we get access to the exact component of the system.
So application should make a first call to get UUID list and then make another to get all the components of it.
This is what the above code is trying to do. Do you have a better idea ?
Let's follow up with the discussion in #310, this is getting confusing.

title: Its time to switch Coding style to Clang format
body:
Clang format is most popular C++ coding style: http://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangFormat.html
Benefits:
- We can also integrate this in git using [git-clang-format](https://github.com/llvm-mirror/clang/blob/master/tools/clang-format/git-clang-format) or add git pre commit hook.
- Clang has a [static analyzer](https://clang-analyzer.llvm.org/).
- It will rearrange header file inclusion order alphabetically (@JonasVautherin was this earlier).
- Supports various styles.
  - LLVM A style complying with the LLVM coding standards
  - Google A style complying with Google’s C++ style guide
  - Chromium A style complying with Chromium’s style guide
  - Mozilla A style complying with Mozilla’s style guide
  - WebKit A style complying with WebKit’s style guide

Reference:
http://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangFormat.html
http://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangFormatStyleOptions.html
https://clang-analyzer.llvm.org/
https://clangformat.com/ - Interactive guide and builder.

@julianoes @JonasVautherin @hamishwillee .

comments.body:
I added a script to run clang-format to the [avoidance](https://github.com/PX4/avoidance/blob/master/tools/fix_style.sh) module last year. Maybe the script can help:

```
#!/bin/bash

STYLE="google"

if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <src_file | dir>"
    echo ""
    echo "ERROR: At least one source file or one directory must be provided!"

    exit 1
fi

for arg in "$@"
do
    if [ -f $arg ]; then
        clang-format -i -style=${STYLE} $arg
    elif [ -d $arg ]; then
        find $arg -iname *.h -o -iname *.cpp | xargs clang-format -i -style=${STYLE}
    fi
done
```

One thing, though, is that we probably don't want to refactor the whole project (regarding git history). I guess we would need to keep our current style unchanged, if possible. What do you think?

Yeah, I am also thinking of the same.
I think, if we've any plan to change at all, sooner the better. We can never do anytime in future as the source code is going to be bigger. As it would just change source code appearance for the better. Right ?
What I mean is that instead of going for, say, the "google" style, maybe we want to make a custom style that matches (most of) our current style. Does that make sense?
Yeah makes sense. We can create something similar to http://wiki.ros.org/CppStyleGuide to match our existing style.
Also, Static analyzer can take care of most of the code review effort.

title: Support multiple callback-subscribers
body:
MAVSDK allows to subscribe to new information with callbacks, like for example updates to the Position telemetry:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7244ace0d7b223e8e7618d8736769f4f2a2ef1f3/src/plugins/telemetry/include/plugins/telemetry/telemetry.h#L990-L993

In the implementation only one callback function is registered, and subscribing a second time would simply remove the previous subscription silently:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7244ace0d7b223e8e7618d8736769f4f2a2ef1f3/src/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp#L2075-L2079

I would love to have the possibility to add multiple callbacks / subscribers. This would also lower the chances, that I ruin someone else's subscriber in a collaborative code base by overwriting that person's callback function.

comments.body:
Yep would be nice. Quite some work though, because all of the streams would need an `unsubscribe` function that would take a handle returned by the `subscribe` function, I would say :thinking: 

Note that MAVSDK-Java and MAVSDK-Swift solve that at their level, but not MAVSDK-Python. Anyway I would be in favor of having them use direct bindings instead of gRPC at some point, and therefore they would need MAVSDK-C++ to do that :+1:

Sounds about right @JonasVautherin 

And yeah, the `unsubscribe` function will probably require some thoughts. Especially given that the same function could be added as callback multiple times, i.e. it's used in multiple places that don't know of each other.

I guess the solution will include an `std::vector` or `std::array` holding shared pointers to the callbacks. And then the pointer to the callback is only removed when the last usage of the shared point is gone.

Yeah agreed. I think it would be worth looking into the cookie mechanism that @julianoes implemented for the timeouts. My first intuition is that such a "cookie" could be the handler that MAVSDK-C++ returns when you `auto position_handle = subscribe_position(some_callback)`.

When you call `unsubscribe_position(handle)`, then it unsubscribes the call back from that collection.

Now the annoying part is the language bindings: how does that handle look like in Swift, Python or Java? Maybe it can be just a type `Handle` that contains a `long` (the cookie)? Not sure.

Yes, something with a cookie/handle but nicer than what I did with `void *` that is super ugly, actually.
A `long` would already be better, yes :smile:. Weekend literature...

I started with a simple prototype for a registry: https://godbolt.org/z/hxhxsWc7M

Couple of points that are open:
1. Probably needs to be thread-safe, or have locks around it.
2. Should the callback itself be stored in a shared_ptr and then returned in the handle, so that if you destruct the handle, the callback is also destructed, and a weak_ptr in the registry can be checked and removed? It would be overhead but probably safer.
3. Should be one registry per mavsdk instance, or system, or per plugin, or per function?
4. Should it be a map instead of a vector? This probably depends on 3..

1. I would definitely vote for thread-safe, otherwise we will always lock around it
2. I don't think that's necessary, I don't see why a user would want to destroy a handle :thinking: 
3. I'd say per system. Definitely not in `Mavsdk`, as `System` should be as independent from it as possible. Per plugin/function sound like they will have their own edge cases (what if 2 functions from 2 different plugins want to subscribe to the same Event?)
4. What about a `Map<Event, vector<Entry>>`? What's called often is the `call(Event event)` function, and it applies only to the list of callbacks that are interested in that event.
FYI: this is coming soon in version 2: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1768.

It would be nice to be able to remove only the source build files so that we don't have to always redownload the dependencies (right now I just delete build/ and install/)

**Solution**
For my C++ projects I always add a Makefile to wrap the CMake commands. I like doing this because for every project I know I can run `make`, `make clean` and `make install`.
